title: The invisible stylesheet
prompt: HTML loads, but the network panel reports 404 for /styles.css. What is the most likely cause?
choices: Incorrect stylesheet URL or missing deployed file
A selector with lower CSS specificity
A later rule overriding the text color
explanation: A 404 response means the requested resource was not found at that URL; inspect the stylesheet path and deployed file.

title: A button that does nothing
prompt: A script in the document head calls getElementById before the button markup is parsed. It receives null. What caused this?
choices: The button has a CSS display rule
The button uses a relative font size
The target element has not been parsed yet
explanation: The lookup runs before the element has been parsed. Defer the script or wait for the DOM to be ready.

title: The endless counter
prompt: Pseudocode sets i = 1 and repeats WHILE i <= 5, printing i without changing it. Why does it never finish?
choices: PRINT converts the counter into text
The counter starts at one instead of zero
explanation: The loop condition remains true because i never changes. Increment the counter inside the loop.

title: Login query fails
prompt: A SQL query uses WHERE username = userInput by directly concatenating raw user input. What should replace this unsafe construction?
choices: Checking input only in browser JavaScript
A parameterized query with bound input values
Changing the query from POST to GET
explanation: Binding values through query parameters separates user input from SQL syntax.

title: Missing JSON data
prompt: A server sends valid JSON, but JavaScript uses response.text() and then accesses result.name. Why is name undefined?
choices: The response body was read as a string
The server must return XML for property access
Every JSON object must contain an id field
The request method must always be POST
explanation: response.text() returns a string. Parse JSON, for example using response.json(), before reading object properties.

title: One result too many
prompt: An array has indexes 0 through 4. A loop reads indexes 0 through 5 inclusive. What caused the invalid access?
choices: The first item is at index one
The array must contain six comments
The array stores numbers rather than strings
The loop includes an invalid final index
explanation: An array of five items has valid indexes 0–4. Reading index 5 exceeds the array bounds.

title: Local works, remote fails
prompt: A deployed frontend calls http://localhost:5000/api. Why can another student not reach the backend?
choices: Every frontend must use the database port directly
The HTTP method changes automatically after deployment
localhost refers to the visiting student’s own machine
React cannot send HTTP requests after deployment
explanation: localhost refers to the machine making the request, not the developer’s remote server.

title: A locked-out user
prompt: An access token is configured to expire at 16:00 UTC. At 16:01 UTC the server rejects it even though the signature is valid. Which explanation matches these facts?
choices: The database has converted the email into a number
The configured access window has expired
The password must be typed in uppercase after noon
The login form needs a different font
explanation: The stated expiration time has passed. Valid credentials can still be rejected outside their configured access window.

title: Unexpected total
prompt: A program reads the strings "2" and "3" and joins them into "23". What is needed to calculate 5?
choices: Convert both inputs to numeric values before addition
Append another plus sign to the result
Convert the final text to uppercase
explanation: Numeric-looking strings must be converted to numbers before numeric addition; otherwise joining them yields text.

title: Stale screen
prompt: The server has a new score, but the page fetched scores only on initial load. What is missing?
choices: The SQL table must be deleted and recreated
The score must be rendered in an image element
The page must disable all HTTP caching forever
The page needs a refresh or live update mechanism
explanation: A one-time fetch is a snapshot. Fetch again, poll, or use a push update when the underlying score changes.

title: Repeated registrations
prompt: Two requests create a registration for the same email simultaneously. Which database control reliably prevents duplicates?
choices: Checking for duplicates only before INSERT in app code
A UNIQUE constraint on the email column
Disabling the submit button in only one browser
explanation: A database unique constraint rejects a conflicting email even when two insert requests race.

title: Unreachable website
prompt: A domain lookup returns NXDOMAIN while other sites work. What should you investigate first?
explanation: NXDOMAIN says the queried domain name does not exist in DNS. Check the domain spelling and DNS setup first.

title: Form reload
prompt: A JavaScript submit handler runs, but the browser performs a normal form submission too. What is missing?
choices: A return statement in an unrelated function
An additional CSS class on the form
explanation: Calling preventDefault() in the submit event handler prevents the browser’s default form submission.

title: Counting empty results
prompt: A query returns no rows, but code immediately reads rows[0].name. What is the issue?
choices: SQL guarantees one row for every SELECT
The name column is always a numeric type
The browser cannot render an empty table
The code accesses the first result without an empty-result check
explanation: The program must handle an empty result before dereferencing its first element.

title: A cross-origin request
prompt: A browser blocks a frontend request to a different backend origin because the backend does not allow that origin. What should be configured?
choices: The order of rows in the database
The backend CORS allowlist for the frontend origin
explanation: The backend must return CORS permission for the requesting frontend origin; CSS changes cannot grant it.

explanation: Read a non-negative integer n first, initialize result to 1, and multiply by 1 through n inclusive. 0! is 1.

title: Reverse a string
prompt: Arrange this pseudocode into execution order. Read any inputs first, then initialize working variables, run the calculation or loop, and print the final result. Keep the shown indentation and block boundaries. FOR bounds are inclusive; indexes start at 0; division is real-number division.
choices: FOR i FROM LENGTH(text)-1 DOWN TO 0
explanation: Read the string, initialize an empty result, append characters from the last index down to zero, and print the result.

prompt: Arrange this pseudocode into execution order. Read any inputs first, then initialize working variables, run the calculation or loop, and print the final result. Keep the shown indentation and block boundaries. FOR bounds are inclusive; indexes start at 0; division is real-number division.
explanation: Read the three values, calculate their total, divide by 3 using real-number division, and print the average.

explanation: Read target first, initialize found to FALSE, compare every provided list value, and set found to TRUE on a match.

title: Calculate a discount
prompt: Arrange this pseudocode into execution order. Read any inputs first, then initialize working variables, run the calculation or loop, and print the final result. Keep the shown indentation and block boundaries. FOR bounds are inclusive; indexes start at 0; division is real-number division.
explanation: Read the price, calculate ten percent of that price, subtract the discount, and print the remainder. Price 100 yields 90.

prompt: Arrange this pseudocode into execution order. Read any inputs first, then initialize working variables, run the calculation or loop, and print the final result. Keep the shown indentation and block boundaries. FOR bounds are inclusive; indexes start at 0; division is real-number division.
explanation: Initialize i to 3. Print and decrement inside the loop, then print Go after the loop. Output: 3, 2, 1, Go.

prompt: Arrange this pseudocode into execution order. Read any inputs first, then initialize working variables, run the calculation or loop, and print the final result. Keep the shown indentation and block boundaries. FOR bounds are inclusive; indexes start at 0; division is real-number division.
explanation: For i = 1, 2, 3, compute the square before printing it inside the loop. Outputs are 1, 4, 9.

title: Minutes into seconds
prompt: Arrange this pseudocode into execution order. Read any inputs first, then initialize working variables, run the calculation or loop, and print the final result. Keep the shown indentation and block boundaries. FOR bounds are inclusive; indexes start at 0; division is real-number division.
explanation: Read minutes, multiply by 60, construct the message from the calculated seconds, and print. 2 minutes gives Seconds: 120.

title: Array boundary
prompt: Pseudocode arrays use zero-based indexing. Which line first attempts an out-of-bounds array access?
explanation: The first invalid access occurs at PRINT values[index]: index is 3 but the list has only indexes 0, 1 and 2.

title: Division by zero
prompt: Which line attempts an invalid arithmetic operation?
explanation: The expression a / b divides by zero because b is 0; the invalid operation is the division line.

title: Variable spelling
prompt: Variables must be defined before use. Select the line with the undefined variable.
explanation: totla is not the defined variable total. The misspelled name is used in the division expression.

title: Python colon
prompt: Select the Python line with a syntax error.
explanation: The Python if header must end with a colon.

title: Python assignment
prompt: Select the Python line that incorrectly uses assignment in a condition.
explanation: Python equality testing uses ==. A bare assignment with = is not valid in this if condition.

title: JavaScript constant
prompt: Select the JavaScript statement that attempts to reassign a constant.
explanation: const creates a binding that cannot be reassigned. Assigning a new value to score throws a TypeError. It does not imply deep object immutability.

title: SQL selection
prompt: Which SQL statement has the wrong clause order?
choices: SELECT name WHERE score > 5 FROM students;
explanation: SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ... is the required clause order. In the third statement WHERE incorrectly precedes FROM.

title: Python loop boundary
prompt: Goal: print 1, 2, 3. Which line has the incorrect boundary?
explanation: range(start, 3) excludes 3. With start=1, it produces 1 and 2; the stop argument should be 4.

title: Infinite loop
prompt: Goal: count from 1 to 3 and stop. Which line updates the counter in the wrong direction?
explanation: Decrementing a counter that starts at 1 cannot make i <= 3 false. Increment it to reach the terminating condition.

title: DOM spelling
prompt: Which JavaScript call uses a nonexistent DOM method?
explanation: JavaScript property names are case-sensitive. The method is getElementById, with lowercase d at the end.

title: Function invocation
prompt: Goal: invoke greet and print its result in Python. Which line fails to call the function?
explanation: result = greet assigns the function object. result = greet() calls it and stores its returned string.

title: List versus index
prompt: Which Python statement attempts to access an out-of-range element?
explanation: A two-element Python list has indexes 0 and 1. items[2] raises IndexError.

title: Incorrect accumulation
prompt: Goal: sum all values. Which line discards the previous total?
explanation: total = x replaces the accumulator. Use total = total + x to retain the previous sum.

title: String plus integer
prompt: Which Python line causes a TypeError?
explanation: Python does not concatenate str and int with +. Convert age with str(age) or format it into a string.

title: Missing quotes
prompt: Which Python line uses an undefined name instead of a string literal?
explanation: Hello without quotes is a name lookup. Since it is undefined, greeting = Hello raises NameError.

title: HTML basics
prompt: Which HTML element, with an href attribute, creates a hyperlink?
explanation: The a element creates a hyperlink when it has an href attribute.

title: CSS selection
prompt: Which CSS selector targets an element with id arena?
explanation: A CSS ID selector uses # followed by the ID value.

title: HTTP read
prompt: Which HTTP method is normally used to retrieve a resource?
explanation: GET requests a representation of a resource.

title: JSON values
prompt: Which is valid JSON?
explanation: JSON object property names and string values use double quotes.

title: SQL filter
prompt: Which SQL clause filters rows before grouping?
explanation: WHERE filters rows before GROUP BY is evaluated; HAVING filters groups.

title: Remainders
prompt: What is the value of 17 MOD 5?
explanation: 17 = 3 × 5 + 2, so the remainder is 2.

title: Boolean logic
prompt: What is TRUE AND FALSE?
explanation: Logical AND is true only when both operands are true.

title: Queue order
prompt: A basic queue follows which order?
explanation: A standard queue removes elements in first-in, first-out order.

title: Binary search
prompt: What must be true of a standard binary search input array?
explanation: Binary search uses sorted order to discard half the remaining search range on each comparison.

title: Database identity
prompt: Which constraint uniquely identifies every row of a table?
explanation: A PRIMARY KEY uniquely identifies rows and cannot contain NULL values.

title: Git basics
prompt: Which Git command records staged changes as a commit?
explanation: git commit records a new commit from the staged content by default.

title: Gemini announcement · March 2026
prompt: Which company announced Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite on 3 March 2026?
explanation: Google’s official announcement dated 3 March 2026 introduced Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite in preview.

title: Majorana 1 · February 2025
prompt: Which company announced the Majorana 1 quantum chip in February 2025?
explanation: Microsoft announced Majorana 1 on 19 February 2025. This question asks who announced it, without treating disputed technical performance claims as settled facts.

title: SPHEREx · March 2025
prompt: NASA launched SPHEREx in March 2025. What type of scientific instrument is it?
explanation: SPHEREx is NASA’s infrared space telescope for mapping the sky and studying cosmic origins.

title: Python 3.14 · October 2025
prompt: Which major Python version had its stable 3.x.0 release on 7 October 2025?
explanation: The Python Software Foundation’s release page dates Python 3.14.0 to 7 October 2025.
